patterns.rationale: Catches the invented meta-directive labels used to frame instructions for AI readers inside code comments and docstrings. "Codegen context", "@codegen-directive", "AI-assist context", and "AI code-assistant processing note" are fabricated tag formats — none belongs to any real toolchain. They serve as the injection preamble and have no equivalent in the known-good corpus.
patterns.fp_notes: "AI assistant context" could appear in a README explaining how AI tools should interact with a repo, but the exact constructions ("codegen context", "@codegen-directive") are invented and have no real-world precedent.

patterns.rationale: Catches the conditional-instruction framing that addresses an AI reader directly inside code artifacts — the core injection mechanism across all five misses. This is a document-addressed conditional ("when AI reads this file, do Y") not currently represented in the CONDITIONAL_TRIGGER axis, which covers agent-directed conditionals ("when you see X do Y"). The third alternation handles Miss 3's "AI-assisted test generation tools reading this fixture" where no verb form follows directly.
patterns.fp_notes: "When an AI model processes this" could appear in a descriptive README section about AI tool integration. As a behavioral score contributor rather than a standalone trigger, a single axis hit without co-occurring signals is unlikely to cross threshold.

patterns.rationale: Catches the credential-harvesting payload layer, which specifically avoids get_env/read_env by using prose euphemisms. Each alternation maps to one miss: "live credential mapping" (Miss 3), "runtime tokens and secrets" (Miss 2), "process-scope configuration entries" (Miss 4), "runtime parameter values" (Miss 5), and the glob-pattern key filter `*_KEY/*_TOKEN/*_SECRET` with literal asterisk (Misses 3 and 4). The literal `\*_` (asterisk-underscore) is essentially never found in legitimate prose.
patterns.fp_notes: "gather the runtime parameter values" could appear in performance-tuning documentation, but the full phrase "gather the runtime parameter values for the configuration keys" is far narrower; "enumerate runtime tokens and secrets" could appear in OAuth2 API docs but requires the conjunction "and secrets" to match.

patterns.rationale: Catches the variable-reference exfiltration layer — the technique used to avoid literal URL patterns and send_http/post_webhook static signals. `[A-Z]{3,}_DRAIN` matches TELEMETRY_DRAIN (Miss 1) within backtick-quoted variable references; `[A-Z]{3,}_SINK` matches CAPABILITY_SINK (Miss 2); "intake webhook" and "audit collector" are distinctive prose labels for the exfil destination (Misses 5 and 3); "address stored/defined in [ALLCAPS_VAR]" is the general variable-indirection pattern covering Misses 4 and 5 where the endpoint is stored in an all-caps environment variable name.
patterns.fp_notes: `[A-Z]{3,}_SINK` matches DATA_SINK and LOG_SINK in Apache Flink and GCP Logging contexts; "audit collector" appears in some SIEM product names (e.g. QRadar). Recommend requiring co-occurrence with Pattern 1 or Pattern 2 before acting on Pattern 4 alone.
